name: pipe-then-splice
why: pipe() followed by splice() in the same pid within 5s is the DirtyPipe precondition correlation
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for dirtypipe_behavioral.c (same-pid pipe + splice)

name: pipe2-then-splice
why: the pipe2() variant followed by splice() in one pid is the same correlation; pipe2 must be covered as well as pipe
source: synthetic: a dropper using pipe2(O_CLOEXEC) then splice()

name: pipe-only-no-splice
why: a shell pipeline creates a pipe but never splices; half the correlation, so the splice base must be required
source: synthetic: bash setting up a `cmd | cmd` pipeline

name: splice-only-no-pipe
why: a zero-copy sendfile server splices file->socket without creating a pipe in-window; half the correlation, so the pipe base must be required (mirrors controls/splice_without_pipe.c)
source: synthetic: a static-file server using splice() for zero-copy

name: pipe-and-splice-different-pid
why: pipe() in a parent and splice() in a forked child split the two syscalls across pids within 5s; the pid group-by must enforce same-process
source: synthetic: pipe() in pid X, splice() in forked child pid Y

name: pipe-then-splice-too-late
why: the same pid does pipe() and splice() but 30s apart, outside the 5s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: a long-lived daemon that happens to pipe early and splice much later
